Teen Suicide: Necktie Youth

By: Jane Lipman | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Why is teen suicide in South Africa on the increase and what can we do about it ?

Summary:
Teen suicide has increased in the last five years according to the South African Depression and Anxiety Group. The new film "Necktie Youth " have highlighted a rapidly developing situation . 21.4% of all teens have considered suicide , due to academic pressures, trauma,cyber bullying , family divorce issues, fast cultural change and a lack of coping skills from the young people themselves . Carte Blanche talks to an expert who gives guidance about the warning signs . The piece might open with a section from the film "Necktie Youth " , that is not too literal , and not graphic. From there we talk to the film maker Sibs Shongwe Le mer , who tried to kill himself via suffocation .Sibs explains what happened to him and why he was suicidal. He believes if we dont talk about solutions the situation will get worse . We focus on prevention and show Cassey Chambers from South African Depression and Anxiety group , working in a high school in Johannesburg , talking to school students about the issue , and explaining what actions the young people need to take . We film the question and answer, and show how upbeat and positive SADAG are as they approach this tough situation .We can interview one of the celebrity ambassadors speaking out about teen suicide , DJ Fresh , who also had suicidal thoughts . We can interview a parent, Diane, who's child committed suicide and works at SADAG .The short piece could use three sections from Necktie Youth to add drama , and talk to Dr Neil Amoore , a clinical psychologist who specialises in teens .He says parents and teens arent coping and the causes are neurological too.He gives teenagers coping mechanisms and he says he has been in practise for 20 years and this is the worst its been.So the piece mainly focuses on Sibs , DJ Fresh and a parent via SADAG and Dr Neil Amoore .The tone will upbeat and preventative , providing solutions and we may include a teenage actor as requested by GM

Press Release:


Teen Suicide
With end-of-year exams underway, could your teenager perhaps be giving you tell-tale signs of depression? One in five South African teenagers has considered suicide and experts warn that young people are under increasing pressure to perform. Parents of teens who took their lives and teens who have attempted suicide reveal the critical signs parents should look out for to prevent such desperate actions. Carte Blanche asks – is anyone listening to our youth?


Script:


NECK TIE YOUTH
TSHEPO: 00:00 – 00:27
It was last year if I’m not mistaken when this young beautiful lady within the school premises and I feel because of her past experiences and everything she committed suicide because in 2011 they attempted to rape her and I think she couldn’t help it and she got depressed and everything .
HLOMPHO: 00:27 – 00:53
My own experience is that four months ago, in the same street that I live, there’s a boy who committed suicide, he was found at his father’s garage hanging there, when the police came as normal they would come to do some investigations to come see what is the cause, it was found that the boy suffered from physical abuse from his father.
BONGANI’ S LINK : 00:54 – 01:08
There’s never been a better time to be young in South Africa, we’ve attained political freedoms and our country has taken its rightful place amongst the nations of the world, yet more than ever, our youths are troubled.
FROM THE PRESSURES OF SOCIAL MEDIA TO ACADEMIC STRESSES , TO SEPARATED FAMILIES , SOME TEENS ARE RESPONDING BY TAKING THEIR OWN LIVES
EXCERPT FROM NECKTIE YOUTH : 01: 08 -01:34 ADD SOUND UP DIALOGUE HERE
SIYABONGA (SIBS): 01: 34 – 01:43
I mean there were various attempts, I mean I definitely think that the first two were very serious but more a desperate plea for help.
V.O : 01: 43 – 02:06
Sibs Shongwe La Mer is a talented, young filmmaker from Johannesburg, whose girlfriend took her life when he was 14 years old. He tried to take his own life at least 6 times. He wrote and directed the film Neck Tie Youth, which has recently been winning awards around the world. It has universal themes and depicts lost, young South Africans using drugs and alcohol to escape their reality.
V.O: 02:07 – 02:13
PAUSE
Neil Amoore is a Clinical Psychologist who works with troubled teenagers and the South African Depression and Anxiety Group, SADAG.
NEIL AMOORE: 02:14 – 02:39
I think that for example, we got pressures around drugs, maybe a huge number of kids who are using drugs as a method of coping, we have social media, we have kids who are over stimulated and now they’re not switching off emotionally, they’re staying connected with their friends late into the night, we have families that are coping with those same pressures, so our teens have parents themselves who’ve probably been through something similar .

BONGANI’S LINK : 02:40 – 02:51
Because depression carries no obvious physical signs, many people ignore sufferers saying, they need to snap out of it or it’s all in their heads and they couldn’t be more wrong.
DIANE NAIDOO: 02:51 – 03:26
Teniell had a boyfriend, she was in grade 8 and he had passed on the first of May. I’d gone out on the morning of the 27th and Teniell was studying, I was actually getting Teniell a few of her toiletries and she obviously just felt that this was the right time and she committed suicide, she hanged herself in her room. I wasn’t even at home, my nanny discovered her and her grandmom.
V.O. : 03:26 –03:35
DJ Fresh is a music and TV celebrity, with more than 30 albums under his belt and is an inspiration for a millions of South African youth.
DJ FRESH : 03:36 – 03:55
And I was 15 my relationship with my dad was probably at its worst, my mom left to study in the US still when I was 15, my best friend relocated to Norway still when I was 15 and I caught my girlfriend kissing one of the senior boys at boarding school when I was 15, so for a week I was literally suicidal.
DIANE NAIDOO: 03:56 – 04:22
I promise you, it’s like a blur. I remember bits and pieces from the mall to the hospital and all that time I prayed and I just hoped because they didn’t say to me she had passed away, they just said to me she had done this. When the doctor says “Call the time” and I realized that this is it, because I think I had put myself into a point or a state that she was still okay.
DJ FRESH : 04:23 – 04:35
I think kids are feeling alone you know, parents still don’t talk to their kids. So whether it’s about just their general well being or about the proverbial birds and the bees, kids are on their own.
BONGANI : 04:36 – 04:52
Where are you? Are you alone in the house? What kind of work do you do? The questions most frequently asked by the SADAG councillors aren’t the ones you’d think would deal with depression but sometimes, all the person on the other line needs is someone to talk to.
CASSEY CHAMBERS : 05:01 – 05:23
We get lots of calls to say, my friend is really not coping she’s been going through this and this, how do I help them? So we want to equip people in the community to pick up on these signs, to reach out and say I’m noticing something is wrong let’s talk about it, what’s going on?


SIBS SHONGWE: 05: 23 – 05:28
What makes someone get to the point where they feel that they can’t live anymore, you know what I mean? That’s a desperate act.
DJ FRESH: 05:29 – 05:44
I’ve been there, I’ve been in that dark spot where I felt like its hopeless, I want out and there are options, there are people you can talk to, it’s never hopeless .
DIANE NAIDOO: 05: 45 – 05:55
I can tell you now they give you the signs, definitely they leave clues, it’s almost like they want help but they don’t know how to ask. She started giving little things away , she clinged to certain people , it was noticeable , but I just didn’t know these signs .
Bongani : Have you forgiven her ?
Diane” How do you forgive someone that chooses to leave you ? that makes the conscious decision that today , I am leaving my mom .”
NEIL AMOORE: 05:55 – 06:35
Your brain develops in the first 25 years of your life, one of your critical periods of development is between the ages of 13 and 17, this is the time in which your parietal lobe, your frontal and your pre-frontal lobes, your pre-frontal cortex to the brain is really hitting its straps and starting to reach maturity and its those areas to the brain that are responsible for a number of very important functions amongst which emotional regulation, reasoning, judgement, decision making and crucially of course the capacity to understand where you are in terms of your own life and what it is you need to do and if those processes aren’t fully developed and we’re now exposing a teen to all of these substances, to all of these pressures, they’re going to make difficult decisions.
V.O. : 06:36 – 06:44
One in five South African teenagers have considered suicide. And now rejection on social media for teenagers feels like rejection in real life . To counter this SADAG works by talking to learners in schools.
SHORT CLIP NECKTIE YOUTH
NEIL AMOORE: 07:34 – 07: 58
One of the most common questions a teenager would ask his/her parents if they’re given a rule or a boundary being established is why, why would I need to do this? Because their credibility is established through precedent and if you can give them an understanding of what could happen and not coming from a point of view of going “THIS WILL HAPPEN TO YOU!” and judging but going “This is a concern that I have, how do we resolve this?”. Involve the teen in the problem solving method as well.

DJ FRESH: 07:59 – 08:17
Your parenting is put to its ultimate test when you’re not with your child, not when you’re with your child and you know, does your child know enough to know when to do the right thing? To know when to say no? To know to say listen, you know at home we know drugs are not cool.
Cassey Chamber I think the first and foremost is to talk and to chat and to find out what’s going on , what were the triggers that day ? When youre dealing with a teenager they are the most at risk age group for suicide .
NEIL AMOORE: 08:35 – 08:53
Talk to someone, when you talk to someone you activate 5 areas of your brain, if you just think you’re activating 2. As a result of which your brain’s health is better, your ability to reason is better and that works with the neurological development we were speaking about with regards to teens. It actually encourages a better problem resolving process.
CASSEY CHAMBERS: 08:54 – 09:18
Some of the signs and symptoms for depression which we know as the leading contributing factor to suicide; withdrawing from family and friends, always wanting to be alone, not wanting to do things you used to enjoy. For teenagers particularly, a change in eating or sleeping habits, so sleeping the whole time not having energy at all, feeling demotivated, it’s a drastic change in their moods , it’s not just sleeping in on a Saturday morning.
NEIL AMOORE: 09:19 – 09:48
We need to look at the system that they fit into, a teenager fits into various systems, they fit into an immediate family system, they fit into a school system, they fit into a social system within the school, they fit into a sporting or a cultural system within the school, they then fit into a system outside of school, so our view is that the teen has got to be seen in connection with a range of systems and not seen in isolation, so what we would then try and do is to educate and boost those systems in terms of how they would then cope with their teenager and give them necessary coping skills
CASSEY CHAMBERS: 09:48 – 10:05
They also start to say things like, I wish I wasn’t here anymore or everyone would be better off if I was dead. Any of those symptoms of depression you need to be aware of and then act on it, don’t be scared to ask that tough question, are you okay?

NEIL AMOORE: 10:05 – 10:27
Depression is a process not an event, we need to be aware of things from the beginning, we need to be aware of all of the kinds of pressures that these kids face, understand the world, read, speak to people, don’t be afraid, if you need to go and see a therapist and go look, I got a teenage kid I’m not sure what to do, get advice. Understand that your teenager may be living a life very similar to that of an ice berg, the bit that you see isn’t the entirety of their world.
There are nearly two million teenagers at risk in South Africa , and the pressure from social media dosent ever go away .
DIANE NAIDOO: 10:28 – 10:48
If I could say one word that would make a difference in any mother, father or sibling or child’s life by doing this and changing the entire reason for not wanting to do it, I think that would be my main reason why I’m doing this.

PROMOS

BONGANI

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Why is teen suicide in South Africa on the increase and what can we do about it ?
metadata.Summary: Teen suicide has increased in the last five years according to the South African Depression and Anxiety Group. The new film "Necktie Youth " have highlighted a rapidly developing situation . 21.4% of all teens have considered suicide , due to academic pressures, trauma,cyber bullying , family divorce issues, fast cultural change and a lack of coping skills from the young people themselves . Carte Blanche talks to an expert who gives guidance about the warning signs . The piece might open with a section from the film "Necktie Youth " , that is not too literal , and not graphic. From there we talk to the film maker Sibs Shongwe Le mer , who tried to kill himself via suffocation .Sibs explains what happened to him and why he was suicidal. He believes if we dont talk about solutions the situation will get worse . We focus on prevention and show Cassey Chambers from South African Depression and Anxiety group , working in a high school in Johannesburg , talking to school students about the issue , and explaining what actions the young people need to take . We film the question and answer, and show how upbeat and positive SADAG are as they approach this tough situation .We can interview one of the celebrity ambassadors speaking out about teen suicide , DJ Fresh , who also had suicidal thoughts . We can interview a parent, Diane, who's child committed suicide and works at SADAG .The short piece could use three sections from Necktie Youth to add drama , and talk to Dr Neil Amoore , a clinical psychologist who specialises in teens .He says parents and teens arent coping and the causes are neurological too.He gives teenagers coping mechanisms and he says he has been in practise for 20 years and this is the worst its been.So the piece mainly focuses on Sibs , DJ Fresh and a parent via SADAG and Dr Neil Amoore .The tone will upbeat and preventative , providing solutions and we may include a teenage actor as requested by GM
